title: Clarify and implement model version pinning semantics for API/SDK
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Context:
We need a clear, predictable semantics surface for pinning model versions via the Redwood API and SDKs so downstream services can guarantee reproducible inference while still benefiting from safe patch rollouts. Current product asks: allow pin-by-tag (user-friendly labels), semver (compatible ranges), and commit-hash (immutable exact). This ticket defines the semantics, server-side resolution rules, SDK convenience helpers, error conditions, and rollout migration plan.

Goals:
- Define unambiguous resolution order and lifetime for each pin type (tag, semver, commit).
- Make the default behavior safe for single-tenant and multi-tenant customers (no silent breaking changes).
- Surface resolved/locked version info in responses for reproducibility and auditing.
- Provide helpful SDK helpers for common patterns (pin to minor, pin to patch, pin to latest-stable).

API semantics (proposal):
- Pin parameter: when creating a route or request, callers may include a "model_pin" field. Acceptable syntaxes: exact commit hash (40+ hex chars), semver token (e.g. "1.2.3" or range operators like "^1.2.0", "~1.2", "1.x"), and tag identifier (alphanumeric and dashes, e.g. "stable", "redwood-patch-2025-02").
- Resolution order (server-side at evaluation time):
  1) If model_pin looks like a commit hash -> attempt exact lookup; if found, use that immutable artifact.
  2) Else if model_pin parses as a semver or semver range -> resolve to the highest compatible semver that is published and marked "released" in the catalog. Semver operators supported: =, ==, >, <, >=, <=, ^, ~, x wildcard. Range semantics follow semver.org precedence with precedence toward highest matching patch.
  3) Else treat model_pin as a tag -> resolve to the tag's current mapping. Tags may be repointed by publishers.
- If model_pin omitted -> use the route-level default model policy: either explicit default_pin (recommended) or catalog-default "latest-stable". Do not silently prefer an unpublished snapshot.

Determinism & reproducibility:
- Every response to a create-route or inference request returns headers and JSON fields: "x-model-resolved-id" (commit hash), "x-model-resolved-semver" (if applicable), and "x-model-resolved-tag" (if applicable). The create-route API will also return the resolved fields so infra can store exact artifacts in backups.
- For tag pins, resolution is evaluated at request time. To create a reproducible route snapshot, clients must set "resolve_at_create=true" which resolves the tag into a commit hash and saves the resolved pin on the route. SDK helpers will expose a convenience method that resolves and embeds the commit.

Compatibility, breaking changes, and error conditions:
- If the resolved version has incompatible schema changes (we detect via model metadata compatibility flags), and the caller requested "strict=true" -> return HTTP 409 with code MODEL_PIN_INCOMPATIBLE and a diagnostic payload listing incompatibilities.
- Invalid pin string -> HTTP 400 MODEL_PIN_INVALID.
- Pin not found -> HTTP 404 MODEL_PIN_NOT_FOUND (includes helpful list of nearest matches for tags/semver).
- If semver range yields multiple matches, resolve deterministically to the highest patch/minor as per semver policy and include the chosen semver in the response.

SDK behavior (Python/JS):
- SDK high-level helpers: pin_by_commit(commit_hash), pin_by_semver(range_str), pin_by_tag(tag_name), resolve_and_lock(tag_name) -> returns resolved_commit.
- Example (Python):
  client.routes.create(name="llm-summarize", model_pin=client.models.pin_by_semver("^2.4.0"))
  # or lock at creation
  resolved = client.models.resolve_and_lock("stable")
  client.routes.create(name="snapshoted", model_pin=resolved)

- Example (JS):
  const pin = client.models.pinByTag('stable');
  await client.routes.create({name: 'rec', model_pin: pin});

Rollout and publishing controls:
- Publishers can mark a new model version with metadata: {semver: "2.5.0", breaking_change: true/false}. If breaking_change=true, semver resolution still returns it for exact semver, but tag resolution will not repoint "stable" unless publisher explicitly marks it as safe-for-stable.
- Admins can configure a "tag-protection" policy to prevent automatic repoints for protected tags.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- Existing callers that passed a plain model string will be interpreted as tag-only for a limited migration window (90 days). We will log warnings in responses and console.
- Routes created without resolve_at_create default to tag-live resolution; we will add a console banner recommending resolution for reproducibility.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for semver parser and range resolution with edge cases (pre-releases, build metadata, wildcard ranges).
- Integration test matrix: tag repointing -> route behavior when resolve_at_create true/false; semver range leading to newest patched version; commit-hash lookup.
- E2E canary: expose feature behind runtime flag for 2-week canary with internal customers before global rollout.

Telemetry & observability:
- Emit events when tag resolution changes the underlying commit for a route (audit log).
- Track percent of requests using tag vs semver vs commit to measure adoption and target docs.

Open decisions (TODOs):
- Whether to support multi-range expressions combined with logical OR (e.g., "^1.2 || ^2.0"). Recommend supporting basic OR later if customers request it.
- Exact shape of diagnostic payload for MODEL_PIN_INCOMPATIBLE (punted to runtime team but should include schema diff and suggested mitigations).

Docs & rollout artifacts:
- PRD: drive/link: https://drive.redwood.ai/model-onboarding/version-pinning-prd (placeholder)
- API spec stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-spec/pulls/200

Acceptance criteria:
- API accepts model_pin with supported syntaxes and returns resolved metadata fields on create and inference calls.
- SDK exposes three convenience helpers and resolve_and_lock semantics.
- Tests cover parsing/resolution and integration scenarios.
- Console shows warning for un-resolved tag routes and the option to lock to a commit.
